faq.a: Shoaib is associated with the Arabic form شُعَيْب, whose core sense is shoaib; jethro (prophet).

faq.q: What is the origin of Shoaib?
faq.a: Shoaib is associated with Arabic. Shoaib is Arabic شُعَيْب (Shuʿayb), the Quranic form of the prophet Jethro.
Yes — the underlying form شُعَيْب is Arabic.
Shoaib can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shoaib should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Shuʿayb is the Quranic Arabic form of the prophet Jethro and occurs in the Quran.

faq.q: What does Shoaib mean in Persian?

A romanized syllable approximation is shoaib. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Shoaib, shoaib. Script forms are شعيب, شعیب, شُعَيْب, शुऐब.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
